conformance: Inject pre-transfer directory-write failures and compare the returned value with an independently read post-operation disk image.

title: Post-ignore affected state is not a continuation contract
source_section: 033 - CP/M 2.2 BDOS-BIOS Error Propagation and Recovery Semantics
conformance: Capture every public state object before and after ignored failures without treating unchanged or advanced fields as success proof.

title: Physical-error abort abandons the interrupted caller
source_section: 033 - CP/M 2.2 BDOS-BIOS Error Propagation and Recovery Semantics
conformance: Place a marker after the BDOS call, inject failure, answer with Control-C, and verify the marker is absent and CCP recovery occurs.

title: Abort recovery establishes a usable command environment
source_section: 033 - CP/M 2.2 BDOS-BIOS Error Propagation and Recovery Semantics
conformance: Abort an injected failure, then execute a CCP command and an independent healthy BDOS disk operation.

title: Exact recovery internals are not part of the contract
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Compare distinct conforming implementations by public post-restart behavior rather than internal call sequence or addresses.

title: Loader ceiling and overlay TPA are distinct
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Compare the first rejected COM record with runtime writes below the advertised 0006h ceiling using a safe private stack and recovery path.

title: CCP overlay invalidates ordinary RET assumptions
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Overwrite controlled CCP bytes after adopting a private stack, avoid RET, invoke WBOOT, and verify a usable command environment is restored.

title: System ownership is an application obligation
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Test documented accesses normally and treat destructive writes only as isolated takeover cases with an independently retained recovery path.

title: Entry-stack storage may occupy overlayable memory
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Vary entry stack placement; require immediate RET, but require an overlaying program to establish its own stack before consuming that region.

title: Cold BOOT public postcondition
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: From an arbitrary pre-BOOT public-state pattern, invoke the configured BOOT entry and verify a usable A-drive CCP/BDOS environment and valid 0000h/0005h gateways; do not require a particular loader or sign-on.

title: Cold BOOT does not promise blanket memory clearing
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: A system may retain or overwrite unspecified memory during BOOT; applications must rely only on documented post-BOOT state.

title: WBOOT command-environment reconstruction
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Corrupt safe gateway operands and select a nondefault DMA, then enter WBOOT and verify reconstructed gateways, DMA 0080h, and a usable CCP.

title: Residual state across WBOOT
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Applications shall remain correct whether such unspecified state survives or is overwritten; implementations need not reproduce the reference residue.

title: Console-pending state across WBOOT
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: After WBOOT, either loss or BIOS-defined retention of previously pending unconsumed console input is compatible unless the configured BIOS interface separately promises otherwise.

title: BIOS vector is a public runtime ABI
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Invoke documented BIOS vector entries through the configured vector and verify the documented call interface.

title: DPH structures are compatibility-visible
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Inspect DPH-derived runtime structures and verify documented fields required by compatible software.

title: Direct BIOS calls expose raw device behavior
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Compare direct BIOS access with BDOS operations and verify that BIOS behavior remains at the device layer.

title: BIOS implementation details remain profile-specific
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Require documented BIOS behavior while permitting implementation-specific hardware abstraction choices.

title: Function 40 selector and input
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Open or create a controlled file, select a random record in the FCB, set DMA, call Function 40, and verify the target record.

title: Function 40 allocation-block zero fill
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Write record 10 of a new file on a multi-record allocation-block disk and verify preceding record 9 reads successfully as 128 zero bytes.

title: Function 40 is not universal sparse-hole materialization
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Vary allocation-block size and distant target records; applications shall not require holes outside allocated blocks to read as zeros.

title: Function 40 result family
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Test success, exhausted storage, and nonzero R2 overflow with controlled images and verify the corresponding codes.

title: BIOS character services are raw device interfaces
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Compare direct BIOS character calls with BDOS console functions and verify the documented layering boundary.

title: Character devices remain distinct runtime paths
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Exercise each character path independently and verify that the selected device service is used.

title: IOBYTE reassignment is runtime visible
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Change IOBYTE assignments and verify subsequent device operations use the updated mapping.

title: IOBYTE access coherence
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Set values through Function 8 and direct access, query through the other path, and verify configured device routing.

title: Field-preserving assignment changes
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Begin with distinct field values, change each assignment independently, and verify the remaining six bits.

title: IOBYTE assignment does not validate device presence
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Accept valid assignment states while testing unavailable mappings according to the declared device profile.

title: STAT device-assignment semantics
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Display fields, make valid changes, attempt an invalid name, and compare IOBYTE before and after each action.

title: Parameterized disk-structure coherence
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Validate empty, populated, and nearly full media against every public field.

title: DPB-dependent directory allocation-map width
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Exercise both DSM classes.

title: Logical directory placement
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Parse a nonidentity translation profile without assuming contiguous physical directory sectors.

title: Raw-format universality
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Accept distinct declared profiles implementing the same logical interfaces.

title: Direct-structure caller responsibility
source_section: 034 - CP/M 2.2 Memory Layout, System Area, and Transient Program Boundary
conformance: Compare a configured direct read with BDOS access and reject hard-coded foreign geometry.

title: Damaged-directory recovery
source_section: 041 - CP/M 2.2 Direct System Access and Undocumented Application Interface
conformance: Detect/report corrupt fixtures without requiring a particular repair choice; I044 ERROR RECOVERY BDOS BIOS subsystem IG AG.

title: Private BDOS target is not an application gateway
source_section: 042 - CP/M 2.2 Common Software Compatibility Assumptions
conformance: Relocate or wrap the BDOS implementation while preserving CALL 0005h and verify conforming applications continue to operate; do not accept a private-target caller as a general conformance requirement.

title: DRI submitted-command stream
source_section: 042 - CP/M 2.2 Common Software Compatibility Assumptions
conformance: Submit a deterministic multi-command file ending in a unique transient marker; verify ordered execution across returns, exhaustion cleanup, and subsequent console prompt.

title: XSUB buffered-input compatibility
source_section: 043 - CP/M 2.2 Memory and Execution Edge Case Compatibility Semantics
conformance: Activate XSUB from a submission, run a transient that calls Function 10, place a known following record in the stream, and verify the counted buffer and continued command execution.

title: Self-modifying transient execution
source_section: 051 - CP/M 2.2 Hardware-Dependent Software Compatibility Survey
conformance: Load a transient containing a patchable instruction, change an operand in place, execute it, and verify the changed result; repeat at more than one valid TPA placement.
